title.narrative: Multi-sectoral life-saving assistance to IDPs and conflict-affected communities in hard-to-reach and under-served areas of five townships in Kayin State, Myanmar.

description.narrative:
ltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gtMyanmar, a least developed nation, faces challenges with 38% of total population living near or below the poverty line. Long-lasting ethnic conflicts, violence, and discrimination have hindered development and resulted in chronic poverty in Kayin State. The 2021 military coup worsened the situation, significantly increasing the number of internally displaced persons (IDPs) due to clashes and shelling of civilian villages. COVID-19 disruptions, economic downfall, increased prices, food insecurity, limited access to nutritious food, clean water and health services and continued displacement worsened the crisis for both IDPs and host communities. Urgent humanitarian assistance is needed to mitigate the risk of crisis-affected populations turning to negative coping mechanisms. ltbrgt
lt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptfont-family:"gtThis consortium led by MI and two local partners (KRRC and KEHOC) aims to implement an 12-months project in five prioritized townships in Kayin: Hlaingbwe, Hpapun, Myawaddy, Kyainseikyi and Kawkareik. The proposed villages in the targeted townships are characteristically mixed controlled areas with limited access to basic services. The proposed project seeks to provide comprehensive life-saving assistance in education, food security, health, nutrition, protection, shelter and NFI and WASH. ltbrgtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptfont-family:"gtThe consortium is currently active in Kayin State and has extensive experience and knowledge of the region and intends to enhance the community's long-term resilience through a humanitarian-development approach.lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp style="" class=""gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptfont-family:"gtThis proposal aligns with the strategic objectives of the Humanitarian Response Plan 2023 and integrates an inclusive, gender-sensitive, risk, protection and conflict sensitive approach. It was developed in coordination and consultation with communities and key local stakeholders of targeted areas and prioritizes the most vulnerable groups, including children under five, pregnant and lactating women (PLW), the elderly and people with disabilities. The proposed activities are in line with HRP standard activities for each cluster, addressing the self-identified needs and protection risks in the targeted areas while ensuring accountability to affected populations through an enabling environment and existing functioning complaint and feedback mechanisms. lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltp class="" style=""gtltspan style="font-family:"gtltspan style="font-size:8.0ptfont-family:"gtThe project integrates protection measures into planning, implementation, and monitoring across sectors. lt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgtltspan style="font-family:"gt
Collaboration with local implementing partners ensures a multi-sectoral response and follows conflict-sensitive programming and a Do No Harm approach. Protection concerns, including gender-based violence and child protection, are addressed through integrated activities. In the health sector, access to primary healthcare services is provided in a collaborative approach with existing structures ltspan style="font-size:8.0ptfont-family:"gtsuch as lt/spangtltspan class="cf01"gtltspan style="font-size:9.0pt"gtexisting fixed clinics, mobile team and it also include enhancing of existing referral mechanism. lt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-size: 10.0ptfont-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
Within the education sector, activities will focus on safe and inclusive learning environments and promoting equal access for all. Shelter and NFI interventions prioritize safe and adequate housing with separate emergency shelters for males and females. Food security activities enhance resilience by strengthening means of livelihood and offer cash assistance. WASH interventions establish and improve infrastructure, considering safety and accessibility for adolescents, women and persons with disabilities. Nutrition interventions target pregnant and lactating women, infants and young children. Following MHF priorities, the project emphasizes inclusion, equity and overcoming barriers to access. Environmental protection priorities and safeguards are followed. ltspan style="font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
ltbrgt
lt/pgtltp class="pf0"gtltspan class="cf01"gtltspan style="font-size:9.0pt"gtThe consortium organizations are working in Kayin more than a decade and know the needs of the communities through ongoing contact with them. The partner consortium meeting were conducted quarterly and shared the gaps, challenges and way forward. The proposal was developed based on findings from these meetings.lt/spangtlt/spangtltspan style="font-size:10.0ptfont-family:"gtlt/spangtlt/pgtltpgt
ltbrgtlt/pgt
